newsitem.title: UK: Sea Empress set to return to spot market mid-May.
newsitem.headline: Sea Empress set to return to spot market mid-May.

text.p: The Sea Empress, the suezmax tanker which spilled 70,000 tonnes of oil when it was grounded off Milford Haven port in south Wales in February 1996, is likely to enter the spot market in mid-May.
Belfast shipbuilder Harland & Wolff (H&W), which is repairing the 147,273 dwt vessel, said on Thursday the Sea Empress would leave drydock within weeks.
A spokesman for H&W told Reuters: "We anticipate the vessel will leave at the end of April or early May. There is still some work to be done."

Acomarit, the Glasgow-based ship manager which operates the ship on behalf of Seatankers, confirmed that the owner would take around 10 days for trials and agreed that most suezmax vessels were currently operating on the spot market.
The H&W spokesman added that the vessel would be handed over to its owner, Cyprus-based Seatankers Management, and would remain in Belfast while undergoing trials before its first voyage.
The Sea Empress will be renamed the Sea Spirit on its return to service.

Speculation suggests the vessel may eventually join the fleet operated by Stockholm-listed Frontline AB following the sale by Seatankers owner John Fredriksen of five VLCCs and one suezmax to the Swedish company for $357 million in shares after acquiring a majority share in Frontline last August.

Latest reports also suggest Frontline, which intends to dispose of its remaining bulk carrier interests to concentrate on tankers, may be considering a U.S. listing to raise funds for new vessels. -- Paul Berrill Reuters Shipping News + 44 171 542 4087
